transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Gupta (Redwood Product), Samir Patel (Atlas Head of Search), Lena Morales (Atlas ML Eng), Jared King (PM), Ibrahim (SRE)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for production; main concerns: latency, cost, privacy (PII), SOC 2 and KMS integration, and integration effort with their current Elastic-based stack. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, sample data for POC, and a benchmark run.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro - I'm Maya, the AE, and Rafael will walk through the tech. Priya's on for product questions. Samir, do you want to kick off with context?
[00:12] Samir: yeah thanks, uh - so we're Atlas Retail. Our search infra is basically Elastic as the primary search index, we do hybrid ranking right now - tf-idf signals plus some business rules. We're exploring vector search to improve semantic matching for product search and knowledge articles. timeline is Q2 pilot -> Q3 prod if it looks good. key constraints are sub-200ms p95 for web search and tight budget - we can't spike infra cost by 3x.
[00:37] Rafael: Got it. We'll demo Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint and the rerank endpoint that takes a candidate set and reorders them, so you can keep Elastic as the candidate generator, then rerank with semantic model. That usually gives big improvement without redoing your whole infra.
[01:05] Lena: a couple quick Qs - how do you compute embeddings? dims, float16, quantization? and what index tooling do you recommend for the hosted flow?
[01:20] Rafael: embeddings are model-dependent; our catalog includes 512- and 1536-dim options. hosted embeddings come back as float32 by default but we support quantized variants for storage on the backend. For hosted flow we pair embeddings + rerank so you can store vectors in your index (Pinecone/Milvus) or use Elastic's kNN plugin. For the demo we'll show a direct rerank approach where Elastic returns top-N candidates and we call Redwood's rerank endpoint to reorder those results.
[01:55] Samir: can you show the console? and the API call flow?
[02:05] Rafael: sure. sharing screen - (screen noise) - ok, here is the Redwood console, model catalog on the left. I'll open the embeddings endpoint docs. endpoint is POST /v1/embeddings with model param. request example: {"input": "product description"} returns a vector. now the rerank endpoint: POST /v1/rerank with query + candidates. It accepts a list of candidate texts and metadata. It returns scores + ordering and optional explainability tokens.
[02:50] Jared: what's the latency if we do Elastic -> rerank for top-50?
[02:58] Rafael: typical hosted p50 for rerank on 50 candidates with a mid-sized model is ~45-120ms depending on model and region. p95 around 160-350ms. If you need sub-200ms p95, we can pick a smaller rerank model or use caching/prefix caching to reduce tail latency. Also dedicated pools reduce variance.
[03:28] Ibrahim: any batch support? like can we send 5 queries in a single request?
[03:33] Rafael: yes batching is supported to amortize overhead. our API accepts batch arrays for embeddings or rerank; we also have streaming for generation but not relevant here. Batching reduces per-request cost but increases latency, so you pick based on throughput/latency tradeoff.
[04:01] Samir: what about indexing and storage costs? if we store 1536-d vectors for 100M products that's...
[04:08] Priya: yep that's the math customers do. we recommend profile: 1536-d for semantic accuracy; but you can quantize to int8 on retrieval store, saving ~4-6x memory. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching profiles given your query distribution to hit cost targets.
[04:32] Lena: security - how is data retained? we have PII and contracts that say we can't store raw content beyond 30 days, and must use customer-managed keys.
[04:41] Maya: hosted by default has configurable retention and we offer customer-managed KMS in enterprise plans. for the hosted API we can enable no-retention mode for API calls and provide transcript-level audit logs on the control plane. I'll share SOC2 docs - we are SOC2 Type II and support SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[04:58] Samir: do you redact at rest or in transit?
[05:03] Rafael: data is encrypted in transit and at rest; you can opt for envelope encryption with your KMS for extra control. We also support VPC peering for private egress. for truly air-gapped/on-prem we have the Private offering, but that has longer lead time.
[05:24] Jared: can we see an actual rerank example with our catalog?
[05:29] Rafael: yes, I'll demo with a small synthetic catalog to show the effect. calling Elastic mock -> top10 -> rerank. (typing) Query: "running shoes for trail". Original Elastic order: generic shoe, trainer, trail runner. now call Redwood rerank with the 10 candidates.
[06:02] [API call played]
[06:06] Rafael: results now reorder to show the trail-specific items at top; scores included. you'll see explainability that highlights tokens in candidates that matched semantic intent.
[06:20] Lena: the explainability bits - are those deterministic? and are they heavy to compute?
[06:25] Rafael: they're model-derived saliency scores; cheap relative to full rerank pass and included as optional flag. not guaranteed perfect but helpful for debugging.
[06:40] Samir: what about throughput we can sustain - our peak is 400 qps web search.
[06:47] Rafael: for 400 qps if you rerank top-50 per request, that is heavy; we often only rerank for tail queries or personalized flows. Another pattern is hybrid: use ANN to prefilter and only rerank top-10. Also use caching for repeated queries. Redwood Dedicated with dedicated GPU pools is the right fit at that scale; hosted can handle mid-high tens to low hundreds of qps depending on model size. we have autoscaling + burst capacity options.
[07:20] Ibrahim: are there SDKs in Java/Node/python? we run our backend in Java/Go.
[07:26] Rafael: SDKs for Python/Node/Java exist; we also provide curl and OpenAPI. our examples include Java snippets and a simple Go client.
[07:35] Samir: okay let's talk cost profile - how do you meter embeddings vs rerank?
[07:41] Maya: embeddings billed per-embed call (per vector) and rerank billed per candidate scored + token cost for any model compute. we provide cost estimates in the console and Redwood Optimize recommendations. I'll send a hosted vs dedicated cost model sheet tailored to your numbers.
[08:02] Jared: for the POC we want to keep things simple - Elastic for retrieval, hosted rerank for relevancy, 1-week pilot with 100k docs and 10k queries/day. is there a quickstart?
[08:14] Rafael: yes we have a quickstart repo and a postman/insomnia collection. I'll attach scripts that take Elastic topN and call rerank. Also provide benchmark harness so you can reproduce p95 numbers.
[08:30] (screen shows repo link: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/elastic-rerank)
[08:38] Samir: excellent. couple of nitty bits - can rerank accept embeddings as precomputed features? we already compute vectors in-house.
[08:45] Rafael: yes you can pass candidate embeddings and query embedding; rerank accepts raw text or embeddings for scoring. passing precomputed embeddings avoids compute for embedding generation and can be faster.
[09:00] Lena: outstanding: how do we persist semantic differences across languages? we have multi-lingual product descriptions.
[09:06] Priya: we have multilingual models in catalog and you can route by locale. Optimize will analyze distribution and recommend model per-locale.
[09:18] Jared: any production incidents we should know about? SLA?
[09:22] Maya: hosted SLA is 99.9 for enterprise; Dedicated higher depending on contract. we've had incidents in past but we provide transparent postmortems and tracing hooks for troubleshooting.
[09:36] Samir: ok let's run a short live benchmark with a 10k sample and check latencies - can you run that now?
[09:43] Rafael: we can run a quick demo harness against the sample dataset if you share it; but for PII reasons maybe better to run the real run in your infra or with a masked dump. we can run a synthetic now to show p95 numbers.
[09:58] (Rafael runs a synthetic benchmark)
[10:10] Rafael: synthetic results: rerank top-10 with medium model: p50 32ms p95 112ms; embeddings per doc 8ms. note synthetic in our region. real numbers may vary.
[10:26] Ibrahim: fine, we need to replicate this in our cloud region.
[10:30] Rafael: we'll run the benchmark template in your region as part of the POC.
[10:38] Samir: ok, security again - can you share the SOC2 + KMS doc?
[10:42] Maya: yes, will send. also we'll include the hosted data retention toggles and audit log export instructions.
[10:50] Jared: for implementation, we plan a small integration: Elastic top-50 -> Redwood rerank top-10 -> UI. timeline: POC 1 week, internal validation 2 weeks, prod by end of Q2 if all good.
[11:05] Maya: great. to recap next steps: Maya sends pricing and security pack; Rafael shares quickstart and benchmark harness; Atlas shares sample 100k docs; schedule follow-up next Wednesday.
[11:20] Samir: makes sense. any objections from the team?
[11:25] Lena: none. Curious about cost but will see pricing.
[11:28] Ibrahim: will validate VPC options with infra.
[11:31] Maya: ok thanks all. we'll follow up via email with the assets.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors: speaker labels may shift; minor mis-hearings (e.g., "kms" as "K M S"), and product names sometimes abbreviated. References: quickstart repo link and benchmark harness were shared in-chat.

End of transcript.
